IR.rationale: A steepening curve signals improving growth expectations and easier policy relative to the long end. That favours carry, credit and equity-sensitive hedge-fund strategies.

B.rationale: Credit-spread changes are a core Fung-Hsieh risk factor. Stable or falling high-yield and EM corporate yields mark easy credit conditions that support event-driven, distressed and arbitrage returns.

V.rationale: Elevated implied volatility raises the premia earned by liquidity-providing and arbitrage strategies, so expected returns are higher after high-VIX months.

AP.rationale: Hedge-fund returns carry equity beta and react to the market with a lag because of stale pricing of illiquid holdings. Strong recent market returns therefore carry into subsequent index returns.

TF.rationale: Low payoffs on the equity trend-following straddle indicate an orderly, non-crisis equity market. That environment suits most directional and relative-value strategies.

ST.rationale: A well-behaved momentum factor indicates persistent cross-sectional trends that long/short and trend strategies exploit, with no crowded-unwind conditions.

FX.rationale: A strong AUD together with a weak yen is the classic risk-on carry state. It goes with abundant funding liquidity and positive returns for leveraged strategies.

COM.rationale: Rising copper signals global growth momentum, which supports macro, EM and equity-linked strategies.

MC.rationale: Loose financial conditions mean ample funding liquidity and leverage. Hedge-fund returns are documented to depend on funding liquidity.

ENDG.rationale: Hedge-fund index returns are positively autocorrelated because illiquid assets are smoothed, so recent strong performance tends to persist.

IR.rationale: Sharp falls in bill yields reflect flight-to-quality and emergency easing, which coincide with stress episodes that generate tail losses.

B.rationale: Simultaneous jumps in US high-yield and EM corporate yields mark broad credit deterioration. That triggers deleveraging and losses across event-driven, distressed and arbitrage strategies.

V.rationale: High equity volatility driven by financial-crisis news marks systemic stress, when hedge-fund correlations rise and forced liquidations cause large losses.

AP.rationale: Weak recent equity returns, transmitted with a lag through stale pricing and beta, raise the probability of a large subsequent drawdown.

TF.rationale: High equity trend-straddle payoffs occur in large, persistent equity moves, typically crashes, which are the states in which short-volatility-like hedge-fund strategies suffer.

ST.rationale: Momentum breakdowns signal crowded-trade unwinds and regime turns that produce tail losses for equity long/short and quant strategies.

FX.rationale: A falling AUD together with a strengthening yen is a carry unwind, a hallmark of global deleveraging and liquidity spirals.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity price declines signal global demand shocks that hit macro, EM and energy-heavy event-driven books.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress indicates funding illiquidity and margin pressure, which make extreme hedge-fund losses more likely.

ENDG.rationale: Smoothed returns and redemption-driven fire sales make losses cluster, so poor recent performance raises the probability of a further tail loss.

IR.rationale: Falling short rates reflect monetary easing, which tends to precede sharp recoveries in risk assets and in strategies with credit or equity exposure.

B.rationale: Falling high-yield and EM corporate yields mark a credit rally, the state in which distressed, event-driven and convertible strategies post their largest gains.

V.rationale: High volatility widens the whole return distribution and precedes rebounds, so the probability of an upper-tail month rises along with that of a lower-tail month.

AP.rationale: Strong equity rallies feed through, with a lag, into large gains for beta-carrying hedge-fund strategies.

TF.rationale: Strong trends in both bonds and commodities are the environment in which CTA and macro funds earn outsized returns, and such trends tend to persist.

ST.rationale: Strong momentum payoffs indicate persistent trends that long/short and systematic strategies can ride to exceptional gains.

FX.rationale: A strengthening commodity and carry currency signals risk-on, reflationary conditions that favour large gains in macro and EM-exposed strategies.

COM.rationale: Copper strength signals accelerating global growth, which accompanies strong returns for cyclical and EM exposures.

MC.rationale: High stress means depressed prices and wide liquidity premia. The subsequent recovery generates the largest gains for liquidity providers and distressed investors.

ENDG.rationale: Positive serial correlation in hedge-fund returns makes a large gain more likely after strong recent performance.
